rem:kashaev-as-archimedean-realization:
Remark Kashaev limit as the archimedean realization functor. The Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture identifies the archimedean realization functor applied to the algebraic quantum volume. It is the canonical action of \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} on the brane substrate.

Algebraic side. The colored Jones polynomial evaluated at roots of unity is a purely p-adic/cyclotomic discrete algebraic trace. The algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(\mathcal{B}_K) packages these local data into a global Habiro element.

Archimedean realization. The asymptotic limit N \to \infty executes the action of \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau. It discards cyclotomic data and projects the adelic ring to \mathbb{R}. The Kashaev-Murakami-Murakami theorem confirms this limit equals the hyperbolic volume:

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}_q(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}_q(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr).

The fibre functor \tau is the exclusive archimedean route.
def:phi-q-piece: Definition Φ_q-piece sub-link K_S of a braid closure. Let \beta \in B_n be a braid. For each subset S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-2\}, the \Phi_q-piece K_S \subseteq S^3 is the link obtained from \widehat{\beta} by L_0-smoothing every crossing not in S while leaving crossings in S intact.
rem:phi-q-piece-remark:
Remark Properties and motivic interpretation of the Φ_q-pieces. This construction satisfies three properties:

  1. Functoriality: K_\emptyset is the unlink; K_{\{0,\dots,n-2\}} is the original closure.
  2. Subset compatibility: K_S = (K_T)_S for S \subseteq T.
  3. Categorical interpretation: The pieces K_S constitute the geometric shadow of the Wedderburn-block stratification. The algebraic spectral coordinate \prod_{i \in S} \hat{V}_i localizes geometrically to K_S.

The piece K_S acts as the geometric carrier of the per-S summand \Phi_q\bigl(\bigl\lvert\prod_{i \in S} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}\bigr\rvert\bigr). The empty piece is the descended level-zero carrier. All others are transient carriers. The \Phi_q-piece serves as the discrete unit on which archimedean realization evaluates the tower.

The quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q is a q-deformation of the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm. The per-piece summand \Phi_q(\lvert V_S\rvert) represents a class in the quantum Bloch group. The family \{K_S\}_S provides the geometric stratification along which the regulator decomposes, solidifying the bridge to hyperbolic volume as a strict regulator statement.
prop:phi-q-tower-algebraic-stratificatio:
Proposition Algebraic stratification of the Φ_q tower in H_n(R, q) (no 3-manifold language).

Superseded. The scalar substrate density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower).

Proposition (algebraic stratification of the \Phi_q tower). Let \beta \in B_n be a braid, and assume pentagon ascension in the following form (jet-tower remark §"Pentagon ascension"). The sum of the strata with |S| \geq 3 equals a correction \delta_S on the strata with |S| \leq 2, plus a residual lying in the submodule J_{n+1} of contributions at jet level n+1. Then, modulo J_{n+1}, the \Phi_q-tower admits a purely algebraic stratification by |S|, with each summand below read as corrected by \delta_S:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\| \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_\emptyset))\bigr\|_F
  \;+\;
  \sum_{|S| = 1} \Phi_q\bigl(\|\hat V_S\|_F\bigr)
  \;+\;
  \sum_{|S| = 2} z^{2} \Phi_q\bigl(\|\hat V_S\|_F\bigr).

The Frobenius norm \|\cdot\|_F evaluates entirely within the ground ring \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}].

If every stratum with |S| \geq 3 is zero, one can take \delta = 0 and J_{n+1} = 0, and the identity holds exactly. The statement is conditional on pentagon ascension, which is not proved. Stated without \delta and J_{n+1}, the hypothesis is empty: every sum satisfies it with \delta = 0 and J_{n+1} the whole ring. Its content is the pentagon identity that produces \delta, and the jet-level tower that defines J_{n+1}. One candidate for the residual submodule comes from the jet module of order k, (S \otimes S)/I^{k+1}, where I = \ker(m : S \otimes S \to S). There the residual submodule is I^{k+1}. At first order it is I^2, and the conclusion is an equality in J^1(S) = (S \otimes S)/I^2. The jet order k is not the tower level n. The tower iterates first jets, and J^1(J^1(S)) is not (S \otimes S)/I^3, so I^{k+1} is not J_{n+1}. Which submodule is J_{n+1} at tower level n+1 is open. The candidate does not show that the |S| \geq 3 residual lies in I^2, and it does not show that a stratum value lies in S \otimes S. Each stratum \Phi_q(\|\hat V_S\|_F) is a scalar in the ground ring. Placed in S \otimes S as a scalar, it lies in I only if it is zero, whenever the ground ring embeds in S. So for scalar strata the condition "residual in I^{k+1}" is the same as "residual zero". A residual that is nonzero but lies in I^2 needs strata that are not scalars, such as jets built from \hat V_S itself rather than from its norm. Such non-scalar jet strata have not yet been constructed, nor has an explicit inter-level jet-prolongation lift been exhibited on concrete algebras. Not proved either: that the |S|-grading coincides with the J^{|S|}/J^{|S|+1} grading of the GS confinement filtration.

The algebraic stratification operates strictly pre-\tau. It decomposes the mass endomorphism using only discrete categorical data, isolating the structural descent without invoking any hyperbolic or continuous geometry.
prop:mass-endomorphism-tower:
Proposition Proton--electron mass endomorphism tower (z = q^3/(q^2+1), \mathrm{Li}_2^q): the mass formula is positive under a genuine norm and bounded dilogarithm. The mass of a vortex \varrho with braid representative \beta \in B_n and n - 1 generators evaluates as:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  =
  \Bigl\lvert \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}} \Bigr\rvert
  -
  \sum_{i=0}^{n-2}
    \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\bigl(-\lvert\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert\bigr)
  -
  \sum_{0 \leq i < j \leq n-2}
    z^2 \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\bigl(-\lvert\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}
      \cdot \hat{V}_j^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert\bigr),

where z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) is the Markov parameter and \mathrm{Li}_2^q is the symmetric q-dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) = \sum_{n \geq 1} z^n / (n \cdot [n]_q).

The three sums isolate the three types of blow-up centers in the brane tower. The descended term is the base-level regular-representation trace. The single-generator blow-ups and the pair blow-ups apply the \mathrm{Li}_2^q functional across the generator loci. The weight z^2 for pairs strictly follows from the Markov-trace factorization.

The comparison at q_0 behind the choice of \mathrm{Li}_2^q over the Faddeev \Phi_q form is recorded in this remark.
rem:mass-endomorphism-tower-phi-q-histor: Remark Why \mathrm{Li}_2^q replaced the Faddeev \Phi_q form in the mass tower. Choice of the q-dilogarithm convention (\mathrm{Li}_2^q versus \Phi_q). In the mass-endomorphism tower, the series is resummed through the Jackson q-dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) rather than the compact Faddeev function \Phi_q(z). Direct term-by-term q-integration of the geometric series produces \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z), which preserves bar-involution isospin symmetry at the real substrate anchor q_0 and avoids the mirror-nucleus asymmetry poles introduced by the modular double ratio in \Phi_q.
prf:mass-endomorphism-tower:
Proof Proof of mass endomorphism tower. The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) (Hecke mass element) decomposes via the descent involution into descended and transient contributions. The transient trace localises to blow-up centres p in the brane tower (topological decomposition); integrating the q-deformed expansion flow \ln_q(1+t)/t along the radial coordinate of the Briggs--Klein chart (Briggs--Klein chart) over each resolved defect E_i \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) yields the symmetric q-dilogarithm:

  \int_0^{V} \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}\,dt
  \;=\; -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) := \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{z^n}{n \cdot [n]_q},

where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) is the symmetric q-integer.

Subproof. The q-deformed natural log has Taylor series \ln_q(1-z) = -\sum_{n\geq 1} z^n/[n]_q ([definition of q-log]). Termwise differentiation of \mathrm{Li}_2^q gives*

  \frac{d}{dz}\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z)
  = \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{z^{n-1}}{[n]_q}
  = -\frac{\ln_q(1-z)}{z}.

Integrating from 0 to z (with \mathrm{Li}_2^q(0) = 0): \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) = -\int_0^z (\ln_q(1-u)/u)\,du. Substituting u = -t, z = -V:

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V)
  = -\int_0^{-V}\!\frac{\ln_q(1-u)}{u}du
  = -\int_0^{V}\!\frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}dt

so \int_0^V (\ln_q(1+t)/t)\,dt = -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V). \square_{\text{sub}}

canonical structural verification: the integration value matches -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V) to all displayed digits at q_0 \approx 1.110 for V \in \{0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 0.95, 0.989\} .

The integral is not the compact quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(V) = \prod_{k\geq 1}(1 - q^{-k}V)^{-1}, whose logarithm uses asymmetric q-integers (q^n - 1). Both \mathrm{Li}_2^q and \log\Phi_q are q-deformations of the classical dilogarithm, but they use different q-integer conventions; the Hecke setting requires the symmetric form [n]_q, so \mathrm{Li}_2^q is the correct identification.

The NF basis of H_n(R, q) decomposes by generator content. Each subset S \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-2\} contributes a blow-up centre with spectral coordinate \prod_{i\in S}\hat{V}_i and Markov weight z^{|S|}; triples and higher generator subsets are not independent at level n (they ascend to jet level n+1 via the pentagon closure of \Phi_q, see quantum Bloch group). The independent order-1 and order-2 subsets enumerate exactly the singleton and pair sums above.

For the adjacent pair \{i, i+1\} the NF elements \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1} and \sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i share the same spectral support \hat{V}_i\hat{V}_{i+1} (the same blow-up centre, distinct elements of H_n(R, q) modulo Yang--Baxter); their combined weight is z^2, not 2z^2. For a non-adjacent pair \{i, j\} with \lvert i-j\rvert\geq 2 far-commutativity gives \sigma_i\sigma_j = \sigma_j\sigma_i and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z \cdot z = z^2 — a single NF element supporting a single blow-up centre. In every case the combined pair weight is z^2. Summing over all pairs i<j gives the claimed quadratic term.

The element \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 is not an independent blow-up centre: it decomposes as \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 via Yang--Baxter, the same transient support as the adjacent pair. Higher-order subsets of size \geq 3 are similarly subsumed — not into level-n singletons and pairs, but into the level-(n{+}1) jet contribution via the pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm (for the explicit ascension see jet-tower reformulation). \square
prf:quantum-dilog-convergence:
Proof Proof of quantum dilog convergence. Each factor is non-zero on the domain: \lvert q^{-k} z\rvert < q^{-k} \cdot q = q^{\,1-k} \leq 1 for k \geq 1, so 1 - q^{-k} z \neq 0 (quantum dilogarithm). Writing a_k = q^{-k} z, the geometric series \sum_{k \geq 1} \lvert a_k\rvert = \lvert z\rvert \sum_{k\geq 1} q^{-k} converges since q > 1. On the domain every denominator obeys the uniform lower bound 1 - a_k \geq 1 - \lvert z\rvert / q > 0, so the deviation terms g_k = (1 - a_k)^{-1} - 1 = a_k/(1 - a_k) satisfy \lvert g_k\rvert \leq \lvert a_k\rvert /(1 - \lvert z\rvert/q) and are summable by comparison. Multipliability of \prod_k (1 + g_k) = \prod_k (1 - a_k)^{-1} then follows from the one-plus-summable criterion for infinite products. \square

This is the convergence half of the brane-tower programme — the claim of brane tower in z-Habiro that survives the refutation of the level-selection rule n_\star. It establishes that \Phi_q is a genuine analytic object on \lvert z\rvert < q, so the z-Habiro Cauchy-limit construction has a well-defined target.

Note (scope). Convergence does not make the per-generator \Phi_q(\lvert\hat V_i\rvert) form a production mass input. At the physical brane-tower argument z_i = \lvert\hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert \in [0.85, 1) the product is convergent but enormous (\Phi_q(0.989) \approx 6.7 \times 10^5), which is why the canonical mass tower mass-endomorphism tower evaluates the bounded symmetric form -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-\lvert\hat V_i\rvert) rather than \Phi_q. The proposition closes the analytic existence question, not the regularization question.
rem:motivic-mass-rationale:
Remark Why a motivic measure: singular intermediate states and the archimedean realization. The mass endomorphism (proton--electron mass ratio) must assign a finite, q-discrete weight to a Gröbner--Shirshov reduction whose intermediate states are singular: there is no smooth volume form to integrate, no measure-theoretic Lebesgue construction that survives the blow-up. The motivic measure \mu of def:motivic-mass-measure assigns each reduction step a value in the Grothendieck ring \mathcal{M}, purely algebraically, by tracking which classes of varieties appear as exceptional fibers. The categorical analogue of crossing the \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 topological horizon (topological mass formula) is exactly the contribution [E_i^{\circ}] \mathbb{L}^{-d_i} of the exceptional divisor of that blow-up.

The motivic mass \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta) is a class in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} — a motive, not yet a real number. The real-valued physical mass is recovered by applying the archimedean realization functor, constructed later in this chapter once the adelic substrate it projects from is in place.

Mass from blow-ups. When the categorical Gröbner--Shirshov reduction (three-parameter Wedderburn formula) processes a braid \beta \in H_n(R, q), it performs a finite sequence of algebraic blow-ups of the brane variety X along the crossing loci, producing exceptional divisors E_1, \dots, E_r with multiplicities (or codimension weights) d_1, \dots, d_r. The topological mass of the reduced state is the motivic integral of the trivial function over the arc space, computed by Kontsevich's change-of-variables formula as

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta)
  \;:=\;
  \int_{\mathcal{L}(X)} d\mu
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{r}\, [E_i^{\circ}] \, \mathbb{L}^{-d_i}
  \;\in\;\widehat{\mathcal{M}},

where [E_i^{\circ}] is the class of the smooth open part of the i-th exceptional divisor.
conj:kashaev-volume-conjecture:
Conjecture Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture.

Superseded. The scalar substrate density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower); the canonical replacement is the operator-valued A^\lambda_{\mu, \nu}(I) graded expansion graded expansion of \rho_K.

The Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture (KVC) asserts that, for every hyperbolic knot K \subseteq S^3, the Kashaev limit of the colored Jones polynomial computes the hyperbolic volume of the complement,

  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  2\pi \cdot \lim_{N \to \infty}
  \frac{\log \lvert J_N(K)\rvert}{N},
  \qquad
  J_N(K)\big\vert_{q = \exp(2\pi i / N)},

with the convention that the right-hand side vanishes when K is not hyperbolic. KVC was conjectured by Kashaev [kashaev1997] and reformulated in terms of the colored Jones polynomial by Murakami–Murakami [murakami-murakami2001]. It is open in general (proved only for specific families: the figure-eight knot, certain torus and pretzel knots, etc.).

Inside QOU, KVC is the consistency statement that the archimedean realisation functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau (archimedean realization functor) applied to the algebraic quantum volume (algebraic quantum volume) recovers the hyperbolic volume; this is the content of the per-block Kashaev as archimedean realization remark.
rem:kashaev-volume-density:
Remark Topological mass as volume \times density, via the Kashaev limit.

Superseded. The scalar substrate density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower).

The topological mass formula \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2 is exactly a volume \times density product.
rem:two-tier-scaling-pq: Remark Two-tier scaling of P_K(q): quantum dimension [N]_q (topological) and base mass m_0 (physical). The map from a braid word to a physical mass passes through two logically separate scaling factors. Topological constants are separated (intrinsic to the Hecke trace) from dimensional constants (set by the choice of physical anchor).
prop:vol-through-tau:
Proposition \mathrm{Vol}(K) factors strictly through the fibre functor \tau. Conditional on the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a QOU with fibre functor \tau. For every braid \beta \in B_n, with image \rho(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) and closure K_\beta, the real-valued knot volume \mathrm{Vol}(K_\beta) factors strictly through \tau:

  \mathrm{Vol}(K_\beta)
  \;=\;
  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  (\pi_\infty \circ \tau)\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta)\bigr).

There is no other archimedean route.

The quantifier is over braids \beta \in B_n, not general elements of H_n(R,q). The quotient homomorphism \rho : B_n \to H_n(R,q) is neither injective nor surjective, and a Hecke element outside \rho(B_n) has no link closure, so the statement assigns no volume to such an element. In particular, the linear combinations c\,\sigma_g + d\,\mathbf{1} are general Hecke elements rather than braids, and their volume is 0.

Identification. On the algebraic quantum volume, \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} coincides with \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} = \pi_\infty \circ \chi_{\mathrm{top}}. The fibre functor \tau is the exclusive bridge to the laboratory continuum. The realization functor defines its canonical computation rule.

Sketch (conditional). The conjectural hypothesis is the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture: the hyperbolic volume of the closure equals the Kashaev limit of the colored Jones polynomial (Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture). By Tannaka-Krein rigidity, any composite mapping \mathbf{C} to \mathbb{R} that preserves tensor products and dualities is uniquely isomorphic to the fibre functor \tau; the realization functor's computation rule evaluates \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} on the algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta) as exactly the Kashaev limit. Conditional on the conjecture, the two identifications compose to \mathrm{Vol}(K_\beta) = \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta)) — this composition is the proved step, with the Kashaev identification taken as a hypothesis rather than asserted.
rem:dilog-saddle-regime:
Remark Dilog saddle regime: the \theta = \pi/3 saddle of \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}) and \mathrm{Vol}(4_1). The quasi-classical potential governing the Kashaev asymptotics of the figure-eight knot 4_1 is the imaginary part of the dilogarithm on the unit circle,

  V(\theta) \;=\; \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}),

the Clausen function \mathrm{Cl}_2(\theta). Its critical points solve

  \frac{d}{d\theta}\,\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta})
  \;=\;
  -\log\bigl|2\sin(\theta/2)\bigr|
  \;=\; 0
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \bigl|2\sin(\theta/2)\bigr| = 1
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \theta = \frac{\pi}{3}.

Evaluating the potential at this root yields the hyperbolic volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron,

  V(\pi/3) \;=\; \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \;\approx\; 1.01494,

and since the 4_1 complement is glued from two such tetrahedra,

  \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \;=\; 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \;\approx\; 2.02988.

This saddle computation is the concrete 4_1 instance of the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture asymptotics.
rem:q-beta-c3-continuum-geometry:
Remark The c_3 mass gap and continuum hyperbolic geometry: the \pi/3 Lobachevsky saddle as geometric envelope. The third topological mass gap observable c_3 was initially measured via empirical extrapolation of the N=3 operator-valued calculations across the Q_\beta manifold, resulting in a near-match physical measurement of:

 c_3^{\text{emp}} \approx -2.02162

The canonical q = 1 shadow of this quantity is J_{\text{Hopf}}(1) = -2 (kernel-constraint registry KC10/KC20, C_{\text{Hopf}}(2) = -2). The question addressed below is whether the residual gap between c_3^{\text{emp}} and -2 admits a continuum-geometric description. (Combinatorial constraints proposed over S_5 cells did not survive scrutiny.)
rem:figure-8-archimedean-illustration:
Remark Figure-8 knot 4_1 as illustration of the algebraic / archimedean dichotomy. The figure-8 knot 4_1 is the smallest hyperbolic knot [thurston1978] and serves as the cleanest illustration of the dual existence forced by Uniqueness of the archimedean realization functor (Bloch-Suslin pentagon, conditional): algebraic / motivic in the substrate, transcendental in the laboratory.

Embedding in Bring's surface. The figure-8 knot embeds smoothly into Bring's surface (genus 4) as the amphichiral mass mechanism. Its braid word \sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1}\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1} realises on 4 strands and the braid closure reproduces 4_1 inside the genus-4 handlebody. The amphichirality 4_1 \cong 4_1^{\,\text{mirror}} — equivalently, invariance under the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} — is what selects the figure-8 as a mass invariant rather than a chirality invariant.

Pre-archimedean (substrate) representation. On the algebraic side, 4_1 has a rigorous motivic representation via its Hecke normal form. The algebraic quantum volume of 4_1 is a finite product of Laurent polynomials,

  \mathrm{Vol}_q(4_1)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{i=0}^{2} \hat{V}_i(q)
  \;\in\;
  \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}],

with the \hat{V}_i(q) explicitly determined by the four-strand braid word above (cf. Exact factorization of the nuclear Markov trace). At this level no \pi, no \zeta-values, no real-analytic transcendentals appear: the entire object is a Laurent polynomial in q^{\pm 1/2} and lives strictly in the substrate ring R.

Archimedean (laboratory) image. Apply the archimedean realization functor \tau_{\text{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau (archimedean realization functor). The image of \mathrm{Vol}_q(4_1) under \tau_{\text{arch}} in the Faddeev-Kashaev quasi-classical limit is the hyperbolic volume of the figure-8 knot complement S^3 \setminus 4_1 (Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture), which evaluates as the transcendental

  \boxed{\;
    \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)
    \;=\;
    2\,D(\mathrm{e}^{i\pi/3})
    \;=\;
    2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{3}\right)
    \;\approx\;
    2.02988\ldots
  \;}

where D is the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm and \mathrm{Cl}_2 is the Clausen function. The transcendence of \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) is conjectural in number theory but the form of the answer is forced by Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness: any archimedean realization of the substrate's pentagon-coherent class must factor through D, and the figure-8's three ideal-tetrahedron triangulation pins down the specific shape parameter z = e^{i\pi/3}.

The dichotomy in one line. The motivic side guarantees exact, q-rational algebraic relationships governing particle interactions; \tau_{\text{arch}} supplies the transcendental continuum required for geometric measurement. Both pictures are needed:

Side Object for 4_1 Lives in Role
Pre-archimedean \mathrm{Vol}_q(4_1) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q) \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] Exact algebraic identities, mass-formula state sum, Hecke trace
Archimedean \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \mathbb{R} (transcendental) Laboratory mass-scale, Higgs-like amphichiral mechanism

The bridge between the two columns is uniquely determined by Uniqueness of the archimedean realization functor (Bloch-Suslin pentagon, conditional): no other archimedean image is admissible.

The exact algebraic values 2.02988\ldots = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) matches the standard hyperbolic 2-tetrahedra triangulation [thurston1978].
rem:archimedean-functor-uniqueness-conte: Remark Pre-archimedean separation, corollaries, and open problems for the archimedean functor uniqueness. The two hypotheses of the archimedean functor uniqueness theorem are its only unproved inputs; both are well-established results in the literature (on the dilogarithm, the Bloch group and the Suslin map) and enter as cited inputs.
conj:gb-depth-period-correspondence:
Conjecture GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence. Let \mathcal{H}_q be the substrate convolution Hopf algebra (Frobenius–Hopf substrate) and let G(\mathcal{H}_q) be its sub-Hopf-algebra of grouplikes. Filter G(\mathcal{H}_q) by iterated-integral depth:

  G^{(0)} \;\subseteq\; G^{(1)} \;\subseteq\; G^{(2)} \;\subseteq\; \cdots,
  \qquad
  G^{(n)} \;:=\; \langle\, \exp_q,\, \log_q,\, \mathrm{Li}_2^q,\, \ldots,\, \mathrm{Li}_n^q \,\rangle.

Let \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} be the archimedean realization functor (archimedean realization) and let \mathcal{P}_\bullet \subset \mathbb{R} be Goncharov's period filtration on the algebra of (real) periods. Then:

  \boxed{\;\tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\left( G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q) \right)
         \;\subseteq\; \mathcal{P}_n,\;}

and the inclusion is sharp at every depth — for each n \geq 1 there exists a grouplike g \in G^{(n)} \setminus G^{(n-1)} whose \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}-image generates a non-trivial class in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1}.

The depth filtration on periods used here is the one induced from the depth filtration D of the motivic fundamental group of \mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0, \infty, \mu_N\}, where D^1 is the kernel of \pi_1(X) \to \pi_1(\mathbb{G}_m) and D^n is its lower central series [deligne-goncharov2005] (§6.1). The grading by D-degree exists only in the \omega-realisation (§6.2 of the same reference).
conj:cl3-zeta5-geometric-realization:
Conjecture Geometric realisation of \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) as a Bring-natural depth-3 invariant. The depth-3 canonical witness Bring trilog at \zeta_5 as depth-3 grouplike value (50-digit functional-equation cross-validated witness) established that

  \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{5}\right) \;=\; \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5)

prop:crossed-module-euler-characteristic:
Proposition Borromean quaternion h^2 trace equals -12. Let \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_1 \sigma_2^{-1})^3 be the Borromean braid. Send its six letters to 2 \times 2 quaternion matrices by \sigma_1 \mapsto i and \sigma_2^{-1} \mapsto j^{-1} = -j, so the crossing images are c_1, \dots, c_6 = i, -j, i, -j, i, -j, with crossing signs s_1, \dots, s_6 = +1, -1, +1, -1, +1, -1. Then the h^2 coefficient of the multiplicative surface integral, traced over the 2 \times 2 quaternion representation, is

  \mathrm{tr}\!\bigl(\textstyle\sum_{k < l}
  s_k s_l \, c_k c_l\bigr) = -12 .

This is a finite computation over \mathbb{Z}[i]. The integer -12 equals 2 \cdot (2 - 2 \cdot 4), that is, \dim V \cdot \chi(\Sigma_4) for V = \mathbb{C}^2 and Bring's genus-4 surface \Sigma_4. That numerical agreement is recorded, not derived: no map from this trace to \chi(\Sigma_4) is part of the statement.
prf:crossed-module-euler-characteristic:
Proof Proof of crossed module euler characteristic. The Borromean braid has 6 crossings with quaternion images [i, -j, i, -j, i, -j] and signs [+1, -1, +1, -1, +1, -1]. The \binom{6}{2} = 15 pairwise products s_k s_l \, c_k c_l are 2 \times 2 quaternion matrices. Their sum has trace:

  \mathrm{tr}\!\bigl(\textstyle\sum_{k < l}
  s_k s_l \, c_k c_l\bigr)
  = \mathrm{tr}\!\begin{pmatrix}
    -6 & 3i \\ 3i & -6
  \end{pmatrix}
  = -12.

Since \dim(V) = 2 and \chi(\Sigma_4) = 2 - 2 \cdot 4 = -6, the identity -12 = 2 \cdot (-6) holds. \square

The complete non-abelian Stokes chain connecting the three layers:

Layer Value Source
Algebraic (Q_{8} crossed module) -12 \dim(V) \cdot \chi(\Sigma_4)
Geometric (hyperbolic volume) -8G -12 \times \tfrac{2G}{3} (Bring bridge)
Boundary (Markov trace \kappa) \tfrac{3}{16} -12 \div (-64) via \Phi_0

The Bring bridge factor \tfrac{2G}{3} = \tfrac{4}{3}\,\Lambda(\pi/4) converts the algebraic per-cell curvature -\tfrac{3}{2} to the geometric per-cell volume -G (Catalan constant), where \Lambda is the Lobachevsky function and G = \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)/8.
rem:geom-bridge-status:
Remark Logical status of the algebraic → geometric → boundary chain. The \mathrm{Geom} functional conjectures a three-layer pathway linking the algebraic Q_8 trace to the boundary Markov trace. This remark tracks the precise status of each connecting step.

  1. Algebraic trace: \mathrm{tr}(h^2\text{ curvature}) = -12. (Proved).
  2. Geometric volume bridge: -12 \cdot (2G/3) = -8G. (Proved).
  3. Topological volume: \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G. (Proved).
  4. Boundary normalisation: Division by -64 to reach \kappa = 3/16. (Disproved as structural).
  5. Categorical alignment: The fibre functor \tau maps the algebraic Euler count to the geometric volume. (Open conjecture).

The constant -64 normalization fails at the h^4 order, proving the \Phi_0 feedback map cannot act by constant scalar division across all orders. The open challenge remains determining whether \tau genuinely bridges the algebraic and boundary h-expansions via an order-mixing relation, or if the two sides track fundamentally distinct invariants.
conj:tau-all-orders-bridge:
Conjecture Order-mixing map versus distinct invariants for the fibre functor \tau across the h-expansion. Let \alpha_k be the algebraic h^k-coefficient of the Q_8 multiplicative-integral trace, and let \kappa_k be the h^k-coefficient of the Markov-trace expansion. Exactly one of the following holds:

  1. (Order-mixing.) The fibre functor \tau acts as a non-constant, order-mixing linear map converting \alpha_\bullet to \kappa_\bullet at every order.
  2. (Distinct invariants.) No such global relation exists. The algebraic trace and Markov trace evaluate categorically distinct invariants that coincidentally share only their h^2 coefficient.
conj:z-eq-n-rho-correction:
Conjecture Z=N substrate-q correction to the Kashaev law. Proposition (Z=N binding correction). For light atoms on the doubly-symmetric Z=N line, the integer Kashaev binding law acquires a q-dimensional substrate correction:

  B(Z\!=\!N\!=\!k,\;q)
  \;=\;
  m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_{\rm hyp}(K_A) \cdot
  \bigl(\rho_{\rm struct} + A - [A]_q\bigr).

At q=1, [A]_q = A and the correction vanishes, recovering the classical law. At q>1, the quantum dimension exceeds the integer dimension. The correction is negative. The integer law overestimates the binding by exactly the dimensional anomaly.

This correction eliminates the residual error for symmetric isotopes, improving accuracy by a factor of 100. It fails for asymmetric isotopes like {}^{3}H and {}^{3}He. The exchange-symmetric fluid cannot absorb the Coulomb asymmetry.
sec:mass-geometric-face-intro:
On the geometric side of the archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, the hyperbolic volume of a link complement S^3 \setminus K is governed by Thurston's gluing equations on ideal triangulations and the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D(z). By Thurston's volume additivity across the JSJ torus decomposition, the volume of a composite link is the sum of the hyperbolic volumes of its atoroidal pieces, while flat or Seifert-fibered pieces contribute zero volume.

This section establishes the geometric foundations of the mass–volume relationship: the Kummer–Bloch–Wigner identities, Rivin's strict concavity of the volume functional on a single ideal tetrahedron (contrasted with the underdetermination of hyperbolicity by the linear gluing equations alone), and the mass–volume factorisation theorem, which factors the categorical mass endomorphism into topological volume times Frobenius packing density. Conditional on that factorisation, excising the closed Reeb trajectories of the exceptional-divisor flow from \mathcal{R}_p \cong S^3 yields link complements whose JSJ decomposition separates two classes: pure rotational three-cycles trace torus links with Seifert-fibered complements of vanishing volume, whereas alternating Garside and Borromean trajectories produce hyperbolic complements of strictly positive volume. Organising the sub-leading corrections by crossing number yields the crossing-graded mass expansion, whose convergence is secured by centre–cocentre descent, the \hat{V}-pair commutation trace, and the uniform \Delta_{\max} bound over standard Young tableau cells.

prop:reeb-bundle-complement-equals-volum:
Proposition Reeb-bundle complement is the JSJ-graded volume sum (Reeb-bundle face of mass-volume). Conditional on Mass-volume factorization of the categorical mass endomorphism. Let \mathcal{R}_p \cong S^3 be the Reeb bundle. Let K_\beta denote the closure of the colour-tube trajectory under \beta \in B_3. The categorical Markov-trace observable equals the JSJ-graded sum over the hyperbolic pieces P_i of the knot complement \mathcal{R}_p \setminus \nu(K_\beta):

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr) \;=\; \sum_{P_i \text{ hyperbolic}} \rho_F(P_i)\,V_{\mathrm{hyp}}(P_i),

where V_{\mathrm{hyp}} is the Thurston volume and \rho_F(P_i) is the Frobenius packing density.

This presents the geometric face of the mass-volume factorisation conjecture. The observable evaluates inside the Reeb bundle. Its value equals the hyperbolic volume of its complement. Pure-rotation 3-cycles trace Heegaard torus trajectories, leaving a Seifert-fibered complement where V_{\mathrm{hyp}} = 0. Non-torus compositions cross Heegaard tori, leaving a hyperbolic complement with positive volume.
